seo.title: Pakistan Household Expenses 2026: What Families Spend
seo.description: What households in Pakistan spend each month on food, housing, transport and more, from PBS HIES 2024-25 data, by city and village and by family size.

h1: Average monthly household expenses in Pakistan (2026)
summary: What Pakistani households actually spend each month, category by category, in cities and villages and for different family sizes, from the official PBS survey, and why cost-of-living websites often show something else.
intro_html:
How much does it cost to run a household in Pakistan? Ask five people and you will hear five answers. The most reliable answer comes from the Household Integrated Economic Survey (HIES) 2024-25 by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), which recorded the income and spending of 32,814 households between September 2024 and June 2025.

This guide sets out what that survey found, turns the percentages into rupees, and explains how to compare your own spending fairly.

sections.h2: Average household expenses at a glance
sections.body_html:
Average monthly household consumption spending in HIES 2024-25:

AreaSpending per householdSpending per personAverage household size
PakistanRs 79,150Rs 13,2405.98
UrbanRs 95,533Rs 16,7955.69
RuralRs 67,894Rs 10,9916.18

Average monthly household income in the same survey was Rs 82,179 (Rs 96,767 urban, Rs 72,157 rural). In other words, the average household spent almost everything it earned. Spending more than doubled from Rs 37,159 in HIES 2018-19.

Remember that these are averages. Many households spend much less, and a smaller number spend much more, which pulls the average up.

sections.h2: Where the money goes: spending by category
sections.body_html:
HIES 2024-25 splits spending into standard groups. The rupee amounts are our calculation: each share multiplied by the national average of Rs 79,150 and rounded.

CategoryShare of spendingPer month (our calculation)
Food and non-alcoholic drinks36.72%Rs 29,064
Housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel25.72%Rs 20,357
Restaurants and hotels6.63%Rs 5,248
Clothing and footwear6.28%Rs 4,971
Transport6.21%Rs 4,915
Miscellaneous goods and services5.25%Rs 4,155
Health3.34%Rs 2,644
Furniture, household items and upkeep3.25%Rs 2,572
Education2.48%Rs 1,963
Communication1.80%Rs 1,425
Tobacco and other drinks1.19%Rs 942
Recreation and culture1.12%Rs 886

Food and the home together take more than 60% of the average budget. That is why the biggest savings usually come from groceries and electricity, not from small treats. Our guides to the family grocery budget and cutting your electricity bill start there.

Education looks small at 2.48% because it is an average over all households, including those with no children in school. For a family paying private school fees, it is often one of the biggest lines.

sections.h2: City and village: how spending differs
sections.body_html:
Urban households spent about Rs 27,600 a month more than rural ones (our calculation: Rs 95,533 minus Rs 67,894), even though they were slightly smaller. Per person, urban spending was Rs 16,795 against Rs 10,991.

The main reasons are familiar:

  • Rent. Many rural families own their home, while city families often rent.
  • Food. City households buy almost everything, while some rural households grow or raise part of their food.
  • Transport and schooling. Longer commutes and private school fees are more common in cities.

Big cities and smaller cities

The published HIES report gives figures for urban and rural areas, not for individual cities. Rent in Karachi, Lahore or Islamabad is usually far higher than in a smaller city, so a family in a big city may spend well above the urban average while a family in a small town spends below it. Use the urban figure as a middle point, not a target.

HIES reports spending per household and per person. As a rough guide only, multiplying the per-person figure by the number of people gives the following (our calculation):

HouseholdUrban (Rs 16,795 a person)Rural (Rs 10,991 a person)
2 peopleRs 33,590Rs 21,982
4 peopleRs 67,180Rs 43,964
6 peopleRs 1,00,770Rs 65,946

Real costs don't grow exactly with the number of people. Rent, the electricity connection and the internet are shared, so a couple usually spends more per person than a family of six. Treat the 2-person figure as a likely minimum and the 6-person figure as a likely maximum.

Allowing for price rises

The survey took place between September 2024 and June 2025. Prices have risen since: PBS put average inflation at 7.05% for 2025-26 and year-on-year inflation at 9.6% in October 2026. If the average household's spending had simply risen by 7.05%, it would be about Rs 84,730 a month (our calculation: Rs 79,150 × 1.0705). This is a rough estimate, not a survey figure.

sections.h2: Why cost-of-living websites show different numbers
sections.body_html:
Crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites often show much higher costs for Pakistani cities than HIES. Neither is lying; they measure different things.

  • Who answers. Crowd-sourced sites rely on visitors who choose to enter prices. They tend to be city-based, online and better-off, and sometimes foreigners or overseas Pakistanis.
  • What they price. They often ask about a flat in the city centre, imported brands, cafés and gyms, not the rented portion, local brands and weekly bazaar a typical family uses.
  • How many answers. A few hundred entries for a city can swing the result. HIES surveyed 32,814 households chosen to represent the whole country.
  • What they leave out. A survey records what households actually spent, including families who cut back. A price list shows what a lifestyle would cost.

Crowd-sourced figures can help you compare one neighbourhood or lifestyle with another. For a realistic picture of a typical household, the official survey is the better guide.

sections.h2: How to compare your own spending
sections.body_html:
1. Add up three months of real spending from bank statements, wallet history and bills, then divide by three.
  2. Group it into the same categories as the table above.
  3. Compare shares, not rupees. If food is 50% of your spending against an average of 36.72%, that is worth a look, whatever your income.
  4. Pick one category to work on first, usually the biggest gap.

Also compare spending with income. In HIES 2024-25, the average household spent Rs 79,150 of an income of Rs 82,179, leaving very little spare. If your spending is close to your income too, even a small cut of Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 a month gives you a cushion for the next surprise bill.

For a ready-made starting point at your salary, see our monthly budget plan for any salary in Pakistan.

faq.q: What is the average monthly household expense in Pakistan?
faq.a: The Household Integrated Economic Survey 2024-25 by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics found average household consumption spending of Rs 79,150 a month: Rs 95,533 in urban areas and Rs 67,894 in rural areas.

faq.q: What do Pakistani households spend the most on?
faq.a: Food and non-alcoholic drinks, at 36.72% of spending in HIES 2024-25, followed by housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel at 25.72%. Together they take more than 60% of the average budget.

faq.q: How much does a family of four spend per month in a Pakistani city?
faq.a: As a rough guide, about Rs 67,180 a month: urban spending per person of Rs 16,795 in HIES 2024-25 multiplied by four (our calculation). Rent and school fees make a large difference, and prices have risen since the survey.

faq.q: Why are cost-of-living websites higher than the government figures?
faq.a: Crowd-sourced sites rely on a small number of volunteers, often better-off city residents, and they price a lifestyle such as a city-centre flat and branded goods. HIES records what 32,814 representative households actually spent.

The HIES 2024-25 fieldwork ran from September 2024 to June 2025 and the report was published in December 2025. Prices have risen since, with inflation of 9.6% in October 2026, so today's costs are likely higher.
